{{nihongo|'''Azusami Tenjinsha'''|阿豆佐味天神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Azusami Tenjinsha''' (あづさみてんじんじゃ{{sfn|Tokyo Metropolitan Association of Shinto Shrines}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Mizuho, Tokyo|arz|ميزوهو|ca|Mizuho (Tòquio)|ceb|Mizuho-machi|de|Mizuho (Tokio)|es|Mizuho (Tokio)|fa|میزوهو، توکیو|fi|Mizuho (Tokio)|fr|Mizuho (Tokyo)|hy|Միձուհո (ավան)|id|Mizuho, Tōkyō|it|Mizuho (Tokyo)|ja|瑞穂町|ka|მიძუჰო (დასახლება)|ko|미즈호정|ms|Mizuho, Tokyo|my|မိဇုဟိုမြို့၊ တိုကျို|no|Mizuho|pt|Mizuho (Tóquio)|ro|Mizuho, Tōkyō|ru|Мидзухо (посёлок)|sv|Mizuho, Tokyo|th|มิซูโฮะ (โตเกียว)|tl|Mizuho, Tokyo|tr|Mizuho, Tokyo|uk|Мідзухо (Токіо)|ur|میزوہو، ٹوکیو|vi|Mizuho, Tokyo|zh|瑞穗町|zh_yue|瑞穗町|qid=Q975797}}, {{ill|Nishitama District|ar|مقاطعة نيشيتاما (طوكيو)|ca|Districte de Nishi-Tama|ceb|Nishitama-gun|de|Nishitama-gun|es|Distrito de Nishitama|eu|Nishitama barrutia|fa|شهرستان تامای غربی|fi|Nishi-Taman piirikunta|fr|District de Nishitama|id|Distrik Nishitama|it|Distretto di Nishitama|ja|西多摩郡|ko|니시타마군|lt|Nišitamos apskritis|ms|Daerah Nishitama|no|Nishitama|pl|Powiat Nishitama|ru|Ниситама|th|อำเภอนิชิตามะ|tr|Nishitama (ilçe)|uk|Повіт Нісі-Тама|ur|نیشی تاما ضلع|vi|Nishitama, Tokyo|war|Nishitama District, Tokyo|zh|西多摩郡|qid=Q1048689}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}.

It is the head shrine of all Azusami Tenjinsha. This ancient shrine stands at the southern foothills of the {{ill|Sayama Hills|ja|狭山丘陵|qid=Q11571728}}, almost on the boundary between Mizuho Town and {{ill|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|ar|موساشيموراياما (طوكيو)|ca|Musashi-Murayama|ce|Мусасимураяма|ceb|Musashimurayama-shi|de|Musashimurayama|es|Musashimurayama (Tokio)|et|Musashimurayama|eu|Musashimurayama|fa|موساشی‌مورایاما، توکیو|fi|Musashi-Murayama|fr|Musashimurayama|gl|Musashimurayama|hy|Մուսասիմուրայամա|id|Musashimurayama, Tōkyō|it|Musashimurayama|ja|武蔵村山市|ko|무사시무라야마시|lt|Musašimurajama|ms|Musashimurayama|mzn|موساشی‌مورایاما، توکیو|nl|Musashimurayama|pl|Musashimurayama|pt|Musashimurayama|ro|Musashimurayama|ru|Мусасимураяма|su|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|sv|Musashimurayama|tg|Мусашимураяма|th|มูซาชิมูรายามะ|tl|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|tr|Musashimurayama|tt|Мусасимураяма|tum|Musashimurayama|uk|Мусасі-Мураяма|ur|موساشیموریاما، ٹوکیو|vi|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|war|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|zh|武藏村山市|zh_classical|武藏村山市|zh_min_nan|Musasimurayama-chhī|zh_yue|武藏村山市|qid=Q390806}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as one of the eight shrines of {{ill|Tama district|Q11430789|qid=Q11430789}}, {{ill|Musashi Province|Q907398|qid=Q907398}}{{efn|These eight are: {{ill|Akiru Shrine|Q11657213|qid=Q11657213}} (Akiruno City); Ono Shrine (both {{ill|Ono Shrine|Q11464224|qid=Q11464224|lt=Tama City}} and {{ill|Ono Shrine (Fuchū)|Q11464226|qid=Q11464226|lt=Fuchū City}}, regarded as {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}); {{ill|Fudaten Shrine|Q11480773|qid=Q11480773}} ({{ill|Chōfu|Q210667|qid=Q210667}}); {{ill|Musashi-Mitake Shrine|Q6587276|qid=Q6587276|lt=Mitake Shrine}} ({{ill|Ōme, Tokyo|Q237683|qid=Q237683}}); '''Azusami Tenjinsha'''; {{ill|Anazawa Tenjinsha|Q11597242|qid=Q11597242}} ({{ill|Inagi|Q317847|qid=Q317847}}); {{ill|Torakashi Shrine|Q11625297|qid=Q11625297}} (Ōme City); and {{ill|Aoi Shrine|ja|青渭神社|qid=Q11662605}} (Chōfu City, Ōme City, Inagi City).}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The current enshrined deities are the following three{{sfn|Tokyo Metropolitan Association of Shinto Shrines}}:
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|qid=Q3275687}} (すくなひこなのみこと)
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} (すさのおのみこと)
* {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q276944}} (おおなむちのみこと)

=== History ===
[[File:Azusamiten-jinja (Mizuho), shaden.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Shrine buildings}}]]
According to shrine tradition, it was founded in {{ill|Kanpyō (era)|Q1346292|qid=Q1346292}} 4 ({{ill|892|ab|892|af|892|als|892|am|892 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|892|ar|892|ary|892|ast|892|avk|892|az|892|azb|۸۹۲ (میلادی)|bar|892|bcl|892|be|892|be_x_old|892|bg|892|bn|৮৯২|bpy|মারি ৮৯২|br|892|bs|892.|ca|892|cdo|892 nièng|ceb|892|ckb|٨٩٢|crh|892|cs|892|csb|892|cv|892|cy|892|da|892|de|892|el|892|eml|892|eo|892|es|892|et|892|eu|892|fa|۸۹۲ (میلادی)|fi|892|fo|892|fr|892|fy|892|ga|892|gan|892年|gd|892|gl|892|he|892|hi|892|hr|892.|ht|892 (almanak jilyen)|hu|892|hy|892|id|892|ilo|892|io|892|is|892|it|892|ja|892年|jv|892|ka|892|kaa|892|kk|892 жыл|ko|892년|la|892|lb|892|lij|892|lmo|892|lt|892 m.|lv|892. gads|map_bms|892|mdf|892|mg|892|mhr|892|mk|892|mr|इ.स. ८९२|mrj|892 и|ms|892|mzn|۸۹۲|nah|892|nap|892|nds|892|new|सन् ८९२|nl|892|nn|892|no|892|nrm|892|nso|892|oc|892|or|୮୯୨|os|892-æм аз|pl|892|pnb|892|pt|892|qu|892|ro|892|ru|892 год|rue|892|sa|८९२|scn|892|sd|892ع|se|892|sh|892.|shn|892|si|892|sk|892|sl|892|smn|892|sq|892|sr|892|su|892|sv|892|sw|892|tg|Соли 892|th|พ.ศ. 1435|tk|892|tl|892|tly|892|tr|892|tt|892 ел|uk|892|ur|892ء|uz|892|vec|892|vi|892|war|892|wuu|892年|xmf|892|zh|892年|zh_min_nan|892 nî|zh_yue|892年|qid=Q30593}}) by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prince Takamochi}}, the progenitor of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kanmu Heishi}} clan{{sfn|Tokyo Metropolitan Association of Shinto Shrines}}.

It served as the chief {{ill|BadSmith|Q135014617|qid=Q135014617|lt=chinju}} of Murayama-gō and was revered as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of the {{ill|Murayama clan|Q11523092|qid=Q11523092}}, one of the {{ill|Seven Musashi Bands|Q11546323|qid=Q11546323}}, who were descendants of Prince Takamochi and part of the Chichibu Heishi lineage. Various theories exist regarding the shrine’s name “Azusami”: that it derives from the {{ill|Azusa Yumi|Q4833134|qid=Q4833134}}, from the {{ill|Catalpa ovata|Q1144805|qid=Q1144805|lt=kisasage}} (ancient name: azusa), or from a {{ill|spring water|Q1881858|qid=Q1881858}}—“Azu” meaning {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sweet}}, “sa” as a prefix, and “mi” meaning {{ill|Water|Q283|qid=Q283}}, thus “sweet water.”

After repairs in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 12 ({{ill|1584|Q6728|qid=Q6728}}) and {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 3 ({{ill|1598|Q6800|qid=Q6800}}), the shrine buildings were restored during the {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} era ({{ill|1716|ab|1716|af|1716|als|1716|am|1716 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1716|ar|1716|ary|1716|arz|1716|ast|1716|avk|1716|az|1716|azb|۱۷۱۶ nî|zh_yue|1736年|qid=Q6989}}) by Murayama Tosa-no-kami. Thereafter, the {{ill|Later Hōjō clan|Q431928|qid=Q431928}} donated shrine lands worth 15 {{ill|Japanese kan|Q116911247|qid=Q116911247}} {{ill|Chinese cash (currency unit)|Q6279611|qid=Q6279611|lt=mon}}, and the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokugawa shogunate}} granted 12 {{ill|Koku|Q855048|qid=Q855048}} as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shuinchi}}. Thus, it was generously patronized by successive {{ill|Seigneur|Q2366336|qid=Q2366336}}. In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}) it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. Incidentally, the place name Tonegaya is said to derive from the location of the Murayama clan’s residence. In front of the shrine stands a shrine-name stele dated {{ill|Bunkyū|ca|Era Bunkyū|de|Bunkyū|es|Bunkyū|fa|بونکیو (دوره)|fr|Ère Bunkyū|ia|Bunkyu|it|Bunkyū|ja|文久|ko|분큐|ru|Бункю|simple|Bunkyū|sr|Бункју|sv|Bunkyū|th|บุงกีว|tr|Bunkyū|zh|文久|qid=Q730266}} 3 ({{ill|1863|ab|1863|af|1863|als|1863|am|1863 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1863|ar|1863|ary|1863|arz|1863|ast|1863|avk|1863|az|1863|azb|۱۸۶۳ (میلادی)|ba|1863 йыл|ban|1863|bar|1863|bat_smg|1863|bcl|1863|be|1863|be_x_old|1863|bg|1863|bn|১৮৬৩|bpy|মারি ১৮৬৩|br|1863|bs|1863.|ca|1863|cdo|1863 nièng|ce|1863 шо|ceb|1863|ckb|١٨٦٣|crh|1863|cs|1863|csb|1863|cv|1863|cy|1863|da|1863|de|1863|diq|1863|el|1863|eml|1863|eo|1863|es|1863|et|1863|eu|1863|fa|۱۸۶۳|fi|1863|fiu_vro|1863|fo|1863|fr|1863|frp|1863|frr|1863|fur|1863|fy|1863|ga|1863|gan|1863年|gcr|1863|gd|1863|gl|1863|gn|1863|gv|1863|he|1863|hi|१८६३|hif|1863|hr|1863.|hsb|1863|ht|1863 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1863|hy|1863|hyw|1863 թուական|ia|1863|id|1863|ilo|1863|io|1863|is|1863|it|1863|ja|1863年|jv|1863|ka|1863|kaa|1863|kk|1863 жыл|kn|೧೮೬೩|ko|1863년|krc|1863 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1863|kv|1863-ӧд во|la|1863|lb|1863|lez|1863 йис|li|1863|lij|1863|lmo|1863|lt|1863 m.|lv|1863. gads|mai|१८६३|map_bms|1863|mdf|1863|mg|1863|mhr|1863|mi|1863|min|1863|mk|1863|ml|1863|mr|इ.स. १८६३|mrj|1863 и|ms|1863|my|၁၈၆၃|myv|1863 ие|mzn|۱۸۶۳|nah|1863|nap|1863|nds|1863|new|ई सं १८६३|nl|1863|nn|1863|no|1863|nrm|1863|nso|1863|oc|1863|olo|1863|or|୧୮୬୩|os|1863-æм аз|pa|1863|pap|1863|pl|1863|pnb|1863|pt|1863|qu|1863|ro|1863|ru|1863 год|rue|1863|sa|१८६३|sah|1863|scn|1863|sd|1863ع|se|1863|sh|1863.|shn|1863|simple|1863|sk|1863|sl|1863|smn|1863|sq|1863|sr|1863|stq|1863|su|1863|sv|1863|sw|1863|szl|1863|ta|1863|te|1863|tg|Соли 1863|th|พ.ศ. 2406|tk|1863|tl|1863|tly|1863|tr|1863|ts|1863|tt|1863 ел|udm|1863 ар|uk|1863|ur|1863ء|uz|1863|vec|1863|vi|1863|vls|1863|vo|1863|wa|1863|war|1863|wuu|1863年|xmf|1863|yi|1863|za|1863 nienz|zea|1863|zh|1863年|zh_min_nan|1863 nî|zh_yue|1863年|qid=Q7701}}).

The {{ill|Azusami Tenjinsha|Q77267791|qid=Q77267791|lt=Azusami Tenjinsha}} located in {{ill|Sunagawachō|Q11587432|qid=Q11587432}}, {{ill|Tachikawa, Tokyo|Q269634|qid=Q269634}}, was invited as the guardian shrine during the development of the area that later became {{ill|Sunagawa|Q11587431|qid=Q11587431}} after {{ill|1629|Q6847|qid=Q6847}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 6), and its main hall was built in {{ill|1738|Q6996|qid=Q6996}} ({{ill|Genbun|de|Genbun|fa|گنبون|fr|Ère Genbun|ja|元文|ko|겐분|ru|Гэмбун|simple|Genbun|sr|Генбун|sv|Genbun|tr|Genbun|zh|元文 (日本)|qid=Q1145754}} 3)<ref name="meikan">{{Cite book|Japanese|author= |title=Tokyo Shrine Directory, Vol. 2 |publisher=Tokyo Metropolitan Association of Shinto Shrines |date=1986-03 |pages=324–325 |isbn=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://azusami-suitengu.net/?page_id=237 |title=Azusami Tenjinsha / Tachikawa Suitengū – History and Origins |publisher=Azusami Tenjinsha |accessdate=2019-12-01}}</ref>. The Murano family of Kishi Village (present-day {{ill|Kishi|Q11475773|qid=Q11475773|lt=Kishi}}, {{ill|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|ar|موساشيموراياما (طوكيو)|ca|Musashi-Murayama|ce|Мусасимураяма|ceb|Musashimurayama-shi|de|Musashimurayama|es|Musashimurayama (Tokio)|et|Musashimurayama|eu|Musashimurayama|fa|موساشی‌مورایاما، توکیو|fi|Musashi-Murayama|fr|Musashimurayama|gl|Musashimurayama|hy|Մուսասիմուրայամա|id|Musashimurayama, Tōkyō|it|Musashimurayama|ja|武蔵村山市|ko|무사시무라야마시|lt|Musašimurajama|ms|Musashimurayama|mzn|موساشی‌مورایاما، توکیو|nl|Musashimurayama|pl|Musashimurayama|pt|Musashimurayama|ro|Musashimurayama|ru|Мусасимураяма|su|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|sv|Musashimurayama|tg|Мусашимураяма|th|มูซาชิมูรายามะ|tl|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|tr|Musashimurayama|tt|Мусасимураяма|tum|Musashimurayama|uk|Мусасі-Мураяма|ur|موساشیموریاما، ٹوکیو|vi|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|war|Musashimurayama, Tokyo|zh|武藏村山市|zh_classical|武藏村山市|zh_min_nan|Musasimurayama-chhī|zh_yue|武藏村山市|qid=Q390806}}), who developed the new fields of {{ill|Sunagawachō|Q11587432|qid=Q11587432}}, later became known as the Sunagawa family and claimed descent from the {{ill|Murayama clan|Q11523092|qid=Q11523092}}. In addition, {{ill|Kodaira Shinmei-gu|Q43594496|qid=Q43594496}} in {{ill|Ogawachō|Q11460543|qid=Q11460543|lt=Ogawa-chō}}, {{ill|Kodaira, Tokyo|Q213278|qid=Q213278}}<ref>[http://kodaira-shinmeigu.jp/ Kodaira Shinmei Shrine]</ref>, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumano Shrine}} in {{ill|Nakamachi|Q119657977|qid=Q119657977|lt=Naka-chō}}<ref>[http://kumanogu.com/ Kumano Shrine]</ref> were invited by the Ogawa clan of Kishi Village—developers of Ogawa Shinden—and by the shrine priests of this shrine, the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miyazaki clan}}, from this shrine’s {{ill|Sessha|Q135009904|qid=Q135009904}}: Shinmei Shrine and Kumano Shrine, which had been enshrined in Kishi Village.

=== Access ===
* From {{ill|Hakonegasaki Station|Q844354|qid=Q844354|lt=Hakonegasaki Station East Exit}} on the {{ill|Hachikō Line|Q1372071|qid=Q1372071}}, take a {{ill|Tachikawa Bus|Q11597871|qid=Q11597871}} bound for {{ill|Tachikawa Station|Q801501|qid=Q801501}} North Exit or {{ill|Akishima Station|Q844152|qid=Q844152|lt=Akishima Station North Exit}}, get off at Tonegaya, then walk 3 minutes.
* From {{ill|Tachikawa Station|Q801501|qid=Q801501}} North Exit on the {{ill|Chūō Line (Rapid)|Q1191297|qid=Q1191297|lt=Chūō Line}} and others, take a Tachikawa Bus bound for Hakonegasaki Station East Exit or Iwakura Kaidō Iriguchi, get off at Tonegaya, then walk 3 minutes.

* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mizuho Town Community Bus}}, get off at Yoriai House Ikoi, then walk 3 minutes. (Route between Hakonegasaki Station East Exit and Ishihata–Tonegaya)

* {{ill|MM Shuttle|Q11546365|qid=Q11546365}}, get off at Mitsugi District Community Center, then walk 8 minutes. (Route between {{ill|Kamikitadai Station|Q6357916|qid=Q6357916}})
